subject: MAP: cost-assumption audit and proposed eval + close timeline
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: cost-assumption audit & proposed eval timeline

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Attached is our initial MAP spreadsheet (MAP_v1.xlsx) and a short set of cost assumptions we used to build the unit economics for the POC. Key highlights:

- Token unit price: $0.0009 / token (inferred from model variant + quantization profile)
- Expected average prompt length: 180 tokens; average response: 220 tokens
- Baseline caching hit rate assumption: 18% (prefix KV caching for templated prompts)
- Batching: steady-state batch size 8, burst up to 32 for warm requests
- Latency SLO: 200ms p50, 700ms p95 (target for interactive flows)

What I need from you to finalize the MAP and the evaluation plan:
1) Confirmation on expected concurrent sessions during POC (sustained vs peak)
2) Whether you can provide a sample prompt set for quality evaluation and caching analysis
3) Your preferred close date / target for handoff to product (we tentatively penciled Mar 31)

Next steps (proposed):
- This week: alignment call to lock on concurrency and sample prompts
- Week 2: we run a short eval with your samples and produce a token-cost sensitivity table
- Week 3: joint review + finalize SOW and sign-off

I opened some quick calc tabs in the sheet — Karthik / Neha, please skim and flag anything that looks off on batching/caching assumptions.

Thanks!

Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP: cost-assumption audit & proposed eval timeline

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for the draft. Quick questions before we lock the MAP:

- Can you break out burst vs sustained token expenditure? Our engineering org expects a steady ~120 qps with short spikes to ~600 qps during peak trading windows.
- Cache: are you assuming cross-user memoization or per-customer KV TTL? What TTL did you use for the 18% hit rate?
- Batch sizes: our infra team is worried about p95 tail growth when batching>16. Can you provide expected p95 numbers tied to batch size?

We also want to confirm who will own the eval dataset. We can share a sampled prompt set but need to sanitize PHI first — we'll target a sanitized bundle by Feb 8.

I've attached a short doc with our SOW clarifying questions (SOW_questions.docx).

Sophie
Sophie Lee
Head of ML Ops, Novalis Health
sophie.lee@novalis.health

Subject: Internal: quick cost-checks for Novalis MAP (please review)

Karthik / Neha —

Looping you both in for a quick sanity check following Sophie's notes. Answer below is what I plan to send back tonight unless you flag changes.

Questions from Novalis and our plan:
- Burst vs sustained: they expect sustained ~120 qps, spikes to ~600 qps. I plan to model two scenarios (sustained and 3x burst) and show per-token $ under both.
- Cache TTL: the 18% was derived assuming per-customer KV cache with a 5-minute TTL and 40% templated prompts in the bundle. If we're conservative, we should present a low-case 8% hit and high-case 25%.
- Batching & latency: my draft batch assumptions: steady-state 8 (p50 ~120ms, p95 ~420ms), batch 16 (p50 ~150ms, p95 ~620ms), batch 32 (p50 ~210ms, p95 ~1.1s). Karthik, can you validate these numbers by EOD? If batch 32 p95 > 1s we should mark it as not recommended for interactive routes.

Attached: calc_quick.csv (small sketch of token/day -> cost), I pulled model unit price and quantization multipliers.

If we agree I'll return to Sophie with: updated MAP sheet, two sensitivity tables (tokens/$ and caching hit-rate), and a recommended eval schedule.

-r

Rachel Kim

Attachment: calc_quick.csv (CSV - quick unit econ sensitivity)

Subject: RE: MAP: cost-assumption audit & proposed eval timeline (updated)

Hi Sophie —

Appreciate the quick questions — we've updated the MAP and attached a short summary (MAP_v1.1.xlsx) plus a two-page calc summary (calc_summary.pdf). High-level updates:

- Burst vs sustained: provided two scenarios in the MAP sheet: Sustained (120 qps steady) and Peak (600 qps bursts up to 10 minutes). Each scenario has token/day and monthly cost estimates.
- Cache sensitivity: included low/medium/high hit-rate columns (8% / 18% / 25%) and how each impacts unit cost per generated token.
- Batching + latency: we validated the batching p95 estimates with infra (Karthik) and marked batch>16 as "not recommended" for interactive routes; batch=8 is the recommended sweet spot for the POC.

Proposed evaluation timeline (updated):
- Feb 8: Novalis delivers sanitized sample prompts (owner: Novalis)
- Feb 9-13: Redwood runs evals (unit-cost sensitivity + quality checks)
- Feb 16: Joint results review (review meeting invite to follow)
- Feb 23: Final MAP + SOW (target sign-off week of Feb 22)

Next steps for you: confirm Feb 8 sample delivery and whether we should model an intermediate close date of Mar 15 (earlier) or the Mar 31 date we originally suggested.

Links: MAP folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_MAPs | HubSpot: HS-94821

Thanks — looking forward to the sample prompts.
